title: Black Friday just set a record — and a warning

lines: they're worried about food and energy.
A record can just mean higher prices
and more borrowing — not more joy.

source_line: Source: Adobe Analytics (U.S.) & BCG 2026 study (Canada), Nov. 2026
caption:
Same weekend, two very different economies.

In the U.S., Adobe Analytics projects a record $12.9 billion spent online on Black Friday — up about 9.2% from last year's $11.8 billion, and the sixth straight record after $10.8 billion in 2024.

Across the border, the mood is colder. In BCG's 2026 year-end study, Canadians say 62 cents of every Black Friday dollar is going to essentials, not gifts — and nearly nine in ten say they're worried about food and energy costs.

Why it's your money: a "record" headline can hide steeper prices and more borrowing, not more bought. The Canadian number may be the honest one — people buying what they need and skipping what they don't.

My take: don't let a record headline talk you into a January credit-card bill you'll regret.

Which camp are you in this year — splurging, or sticking to essentials? 👇

Source: Adobe Analytics and BCG 2026 Year-End Sales Events Consumer Study (Nov. 2026)
